title: Datadog replaces its $0 Infrastructure Free card with a Basic tier priced via Contact sales
snippet:
Datadog retired the self-serve $0 Infrastructure Free card (up to 5 hosts, core system metrics, 1-day retention) and replaced it with a Basic tier priced via Contact sales, aimed at noncritical workloads and mixable with Pro or Enterprise hosts in the same account. A no-cost option still exists per the new FAQ, but only as up to 5 Basic hosts with 1-day retention rather than a standalone priced card. The Pro card's bullets were also rewritten to lead with container monitoring and OpenTelemetry support, with the dashboards and 15-month retention bullets that used to sit there moved down to the new Basic tier.
## Why it matters
Small teams can still run up to 5 Basic hosts free, but the $0 card is gone from the plan lineup, and pricing for Basic beyond that requires a sales conversation. At the same time, the Pro card now leads with container monitoring and OpenTelemetry support, which are not available on Basic hosts.

title: Getting Started with Datadog Monitoring in Rancher | SUSE Communities
snippet:
Datadog has a free account tier allowing you to use their service
indefinitely with up to 5 hosts. To get started, first sign up for the
free trial on [their website](https://www.datadoghq.com/). Once you are
signed into your account, you will need to grab your API key which can
be found under Integrations =>
[APIs](https://app.datadoghq.com/account/settings#api). Also make sure
to activate the [Docker
integration](https://app.datadoghq.com/account/settings) for your
account.

title: GitHub Student Developers & Datadog
snippet:
The Datadog Student Developer program is part of [GitHub Education's Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack?utm_source=github+datadog) and provides free Datadog for up to two years while the participant remains a student.
